Description:
Based on the diff, I can now provide the summary:
Problem:
The current setup requires developers to run entire commands through a scripts/entire-dev wrapper script or have the installed binary on PATH. External agent hooks (in Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, etc.) are configured with absolute script paths like ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/scripts/entire-dev hooks ... or Git repository root paths. This creates friction: the scripts/entire-dev script doesn't exist in released versions, installations fail when entire isn't in PATH, and removing the local-dev mode leaves broken hook configurations when entire disable is run without cleanup.
Solution:
Replace all external agent hook commands with PATH-aware guards that check if entire is available and gracefully skip execution if not. All hooks now use sh -c 'if ! command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 0; fi; exec entire hooks <agent> <hook>' pattern. This eliminates the dependency on scripts/entire-dev, removes the local_dev setting from .entire/settings.json, and handles installation problems without breaking agent workflows. Session-start hooks provide a helpful error message when entire is missing. The entire disable --uninstall flag now properly removes hooks from all configured agents.

content.text:
Reviewed the trail (fetched via `entire trail show` — the web page needs auth) plus the actual code. Verified locally: `go build ./...` clean, `golangci-lint 2.11.3` on `cmd/entire/cli/...` → 0 issues, `go test -run TestRunUninstall` → pass.

## The change itself is good

The core fix is right and the reasoning in the comments is unusually load-bearing (in a good way):

- `external.DiscoverAndRegister` at the top of `runUninstall` before `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled` — correct ordering, and gated-not-`Always` is the right call. I verified the premise: `setup.go:225/655/1275/1925` all persist `ExternalAgents = true` when an external agent is added, so an installed plugin does imply the gate is on.
- Reusing `agentsWithInstalledHooks` for the removal decision (`f36363395`) is the right shape: one subprocess probe per plugin, and what you uninstall is exactly what the confirmation summary showed.
- `!wasInstalled[name] && external.IsExternal(ag)` — skipping only externals is correct. Discovery registers every `entire-agent-*` on `$PATH`, and `UninstallHooks` is a mutating subprocess, so not calling it on unenabled plugins matters; built-ins staying unconditional still cleans up hooks a stale `AreHooksInstalled` misses.
- Printing the recovery hint *before* step 4 deletes `.entire/` is the detail that makes it actionable. Good catch.

## Blocking-ish: the trail, not the code

1. **The trail description describes a completely different change.** It talks about `scripts/entire-dev`, `sh -c 'command -v entire ...'` hook guards, and removing `local_dev` from settings. The actual diff vs `main` is two files (`setup.go`, `setup_test.go`, +175/−6). Anyone reviewing from the trail body reviews the wrong PR. Worth rewriting before you ask for review.

2. **The trail base is stale.** It records `fix/1928-agent-group-external-discovery`, which is now ~389 files / 26k lines behind — and the branch has merged `main` twice since. `git diff <base>...HEAD` is unreviewable. Re-point it at `main`.

3. **The recovery path isn't on the trail yet.** `failedExternal`, the non-zero exit, and `ENTIRE_TEST_FAIL_UNINSTALL_HOOKS` are uncommitted working-tree changes. Two commits are pushed; this third piece isn't.

## Code findings

**`setup_test.go:1355` — the skip test can pass on a broken harness.** `TestRunUninstall_SkipsUnenabledExternalAgent` treats a missing exec log as a pass, but discovery always runs `info` and detection always runs `are-hooks-installed`, so the log *must* exist. A missing file means `ENTIRE_TEST_EXEC_LOG` never took effect — i.e. the assertion never ran. Tighten it:

```go
data, err := os.ReadFile(execLog)
if err != nil {
    t.Fatalf("reading exec log: %v (plugin was never executed at all)", err)
}
if !strings.Contains(string(data), "are-hooks-installed") { ... }
if strings.Contains(string(data), "uninstall-hooks") { ... }
```

**`setup.go:2585` / `:2467` — the same failure is reported under two different names.** The wrapped error uses `ag.Type()` ("ext-foo Agent"), the hint below uses the registry name ("ext-foo hooks are still installed"). Everything else in this output goes through `agentDisplayNames`. `removeAgentHooks` has `ag` in hand — returning display name alongside the registry name (needed for the binary suffix) would keep it consistent.

**`setup.go:2506` comment overstates for built-ins.** "leftover agent hooks … are unreachable from a re-run now that `.entire/` is gone" is only true for external plugins; a built-in agent whose `UninstallHooks` fails is fully retryable, and the early-return guard won't short-circuit because `len(agentsWithInstalledHooks) > 0`. The user-facing text is fine ("see the warnings above") — just the comment.

**Minor: `ACCESSIBLE=1` in a tty-less environment.** `huh`'s accessible mode reads stdin rather than `/dev/tty`, so `printf 'y\n' | ACCESSIBLE=1 entire disable --uninstall` used to work where there's no controlling terminal and now errors. `--force` covers it and the message names it, so I'd only note it — but it is a behavior change for screen-reader users in CI-like shells.

Nothing here changes the shape of the fix; #1–3 are what I'd fix before sending it out for review.

## Problem

`entire disable --uninstall` reaches an agent only through the agent registry, and an
external agent's hooks can only be removed by calling back into its plugin
(`entire-agent-<name> uninstall-hooks`). Nothing in the uninstall path ran external
agent discovery, so a discovered-at-runtime plugin was invisible there: it was absent
from the confirmation summary, its `UninstallHooks` never ran, and its hooks survived an
uninstall that reported success.

## Solution

`runUninstall` now discovers external agents before it takes stock of what is installed,
so an external plugin appears in the confirmation summary and gets its hooks removed.

- **Discovery is gated, not `Always`.** Enabling an external agent (`entire agent add
  <plugin>`, `entire enable --agent <plugin>`) persists `external_agents=true`, so an
  installed external agent implies the gate is on. The gate is the user's authorization
  for the CLI to execute their plugins; uninstalling is not a reason to start executing
  ones they never authorized.
- **Detect once per uninstall.** `removeAgentHooks` takes the set the confirmation
  summary was built from instead of re-probing. For an external agent
  `AreHooksInstalled` is a subprocess, and reusing the same answer means the uninstall
  removes exactly what the user was shown.
- **Skip plugins reporting no hooks.** Discovery registers every `entire-agent-*` binary
  on `$PATH`, not just the one the user enabled, and `uninstall-hooks` is a mutating
  subprocess — so a plugin reporting no hooks is left alone. Built-in agents still get
  the call unconditionally: it is in-process, idempotent, and still removes hooks a stale
  `AreHooksInstalled` fails to recognize.
- **Leftover hooks are recoverable.** Uninstall deletes `.entire/`, and with it the
  `external_agents` setting that gates discovery — so a re-run cannot even see these
  plugins, let alone retry them. When a plugin's `uninstall-hooks` fails, this run names
  it, prints the command that still works while the hooks are reachable, says a re-run
  will not reach it, and exits non-zero so a wrapping script sees the failure too.
- **Usable without a terminal.** The confirmation prompt reaches `huh`, whose bubbletea
  program opens `/dev/tty` directly. Without a terminal the caller now gets a message
  pointing at `--force` instead of a bubbletea internal error, and a `go test` run with a
  controlling terminal no longer blocks on a rendered prompt.

## Scope

`cmd/entire/cli/setup.go` and `cmd/entire/cli/setup_test.go`.

Tests cover: external hooks removed, summary names the external agent, one
`are-hooks-installed` probe per uninstall, unenabled plugin left alone, a failing
`uninstall-hooks` reported with a non-zero exit, and the no-terminal confirmation guard.
